Privacy Support

Margin Privacy Policy

Last updated: November 18, 2026

This Privacy Policy describes how Everlight Digital ("we", "us") handles information when you use Margin: Podcast Player ("Margin") on iPhone and iPad, with its widgets, Apple Watch app and CarPlay support.

Margin collects nothing about you. There is no account, no sign-in, no advertising, no analytics, and no tracking. Your library, queue, listening history and stats live on your own device, and the stats are worked out there too.

Information We Collect

  • Your library and listening data (stored on your device): The shows you follow, your queues, bookmarks, playback positions, listening history and listening stats are stored in Margin's own database on your device. We never receive them.
  • Settings (stored on your device): Your playback, download, notification and transcript preferences are stored locally.
  • iCloud sync (Apple's service, not ours): Sync is optional and you turn it on yourself. When it is on, your library, progress, stats and queues are stored in your private iCloud database so they appear on your other Apple devices. It is stored under your own Apple Account, is governed by Apple's Privacy Policy, and cannot be read by us. Turn it off and Margin keeps working with local storage only.
  • Files you export: If you export your shows (OPML) or your listening data, the file goes wherever you choose to send it. We never receive it.
  • Crash diagnostics: Margin uses Apple's MetricKit. Diagnostic reports stay on your device unless you choose to share one.

Where Margin Connects

Margin has no server of ours for your data. When you use it, your device talks directly to these services:

  • The podcast publisher you chose. Feeds, episode audio, artwork, chapters and publisher-provided transcripts are fetched straight from the host named in the show's feed. That host can see the request, as it can for any podcast app, including your IP address. If you add a private feed, its address (and any token in it) is sent to that host only.
  • Apple's public podcast search. Show and episode search, and Top Charts, use Apple's iTunes Search and lookup services. They receive the search text you type (and your device's region for charts), nothing else.
  • Spotify, only when you paste a Spotify link. Margin resolves the link using Spotify's public oEmbed service and the public show page, with no login and no cookies, to find the matching show in Apple's podcast directory.
  • Apple iCloud, only if you turn on sync (see above).
  • Apple App Store, for downloading and updating the app.

Shared Transcript Cache

Margin can make a transcript on your iPhone using Apple's on-device speech recognition. Your audio is never uploaded. To save other listeners from repeating the work, Margin uses a shared transcript cache that we run on Cloudflare.

  • What is sent when you open or make a transcript: Margin asks the cache whether a transcript already exists for the episode. The request contains only a one-way SHA-256 hash of the episode's public feed address and episode ID. It does not contain the show name, episode title, or your library.
  • What is uploaded: When a transcript has been made on your iPhone (or fetched from the show's own public feed), Margin may upload the transcript text with its timestamps (and speaker labels where they exist), stored under that same hash. No audio is uploaded. The upload carries no account, device identifier or user identifier.
  • Public episodes only: Feeds that look private (a login in the address, or a token in the address or path) are never looked up or uploaded.
  • What Cloudflare sees: As with any internet request, the Cloudflare service receives your IP address while handling the request. We do not use it to identify you.
  • You can turn it off: In Margin, go to Settings → Transcripts → Shared transcript cache. It is on by default. When it is off, Margin neither looks up nor uploads shared transcripts, and transcribing on your iPhone still works.
  • How long transcripts are kept: A shared transcript is kept with its episode for as long as the cache runs, so no one has to transcribe that episode again. It holds no information about you, so there is nothing personal to delete.
  • Transcripts may contain mistakes. They come from automatic speech recognition, and a transcript someone else made is shown to you labeled as such.

Subscriptions

Margin is free to download, and following, searching, playing and downloading podcasts stay free. Margin Plus is an optional auto-renewing subscription (monthly, or yearly with a free trial). Purchases, renewals, cancellations and refunds are handled entirely by Apple through your Apple Account. We never receive your name, payment details or Apple ID. The app checks your Plus status on your device using Apple’s StoreKit, and that status is not sent to us. You can manage or cancel your subscription in iOS Settings → [your name] → Subscriptions, or from Settings → Margin Plus in the app.

How We Use Information

We do not use your personal information, because we never receive it. The only thing we hold is the shared transcript text described above, which contains no information about you.

How We Share Information

We do not sell your data. Margin contains no advertising, no third-party analytics, no crash-reporting SDK and no tracking SDK. Its network connections are the ones listed under “Where Margin Connects” above.

Children

Margin is a general-audience podcast player and is not directed to children under 13. It does not knowingly collect personal information from anyone, of any age.

Your Rights

Because we hold no data about you, there is nothing for us to export or delete. You can export your shows and your listening data at any time, and delete the app to remove all local data. To remove synced copies, delete Margin's data from iOS Settings → [your name] → iCloud → Manage Account Storage. EU/UK users have GDPR rights; California users have CCPA rights. Contact brendan@everlight-digital.com.

Security

Margin runs inside the iOS app sandbox. Its data is protected by your device's own file protections and passcode, and iCloud data is protected by your Apple Account.

Changes to This Policy

We may update this policy. Material changes will be announced in-app.
